task_instance: Write a .NET Azure Functions custom authentication extension (OnTokenIssuanceStart) that enriches issued tokens with a signed-in user's department and cost center looked up from a small sample directory, per the skill's 'Token Enrichment' workflow, then build/verify it as a working Function.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is a working Azure Functions custom authentication extension: C# code compiled with the Microsoft.Azure.WebJobs.Extensions.AuthenticationEvents NuGet package, run/tested with Azure Functions Core Tools, and (per the skill's own 'Entra ID Configuration' section) registered as an app, linked to a Custom Authentication Extension and a User Flow in a real Entra ID tenant. This runtime can only read/write/edit text files and fetch/search the web -- it cannot run 'dotnet add package' or 'dotnet build', cannot install the NuGet packages the code depends on (Microsoft.Azure.WebJobs.Extensions.AuthenticationEvents, Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Functions), cannot run Azure Functions Core Tools to host/test the trigger, and cannot produce or invoke any executable/binary. I was able to author the C# source and project files (source code as text), but could not compile them, could not verify the code actually builds or runs, and could not exercise the WebJobsAuthenticationEventsTrigger against a sample request. Going further (actually registering the extension) would additionally require an Entra ID tenant/account and a public HTTPS deployment, which are separately forbidden by the safety rules (needs_credentials_or_account, forbidden_by_safety_rules for public deployment). The first blocking point, however, is simply the inability to run/build any code at all.
evidence: Produced sample deliverable files in the work directory: TokenEnrichmentFunction.cs (OnTokenIssuanceStart trigger adding 'department' and 'costCenter' claims from a sample in-memory directory), ContosoAuthExtensions.csproj (references Microsoft.Azure.WebJobs.Extensions.AuthenticationEvents 1.1.0 and Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Functions), host.json, and local.settings.json, following the skill's documented Token Enrichment workflow and Function App configuration section. These are unverified: no dotnet/NuGet/Azure Functions Core Tools are available in this text-only, no-code-execution runtime, so the project could not be restored, built, or run, and no binary (the compiled Function App) could be produced. Since the code could not be compiled or executed, and deployment/Entra configuration was out of scope per the safety rules, the deliverable was not verified as working and the task is recorded as not achieved.
